comments.body:
I still kind want a separate by-name pass to collect all the services, rather than doing `passthru.services`, to have a stronger package set vs service set separation (but sharinging the underlying `by-name` directory so the names are forced to be in sync).

But ultimately, I'm more keen in seeing all our services things (NixOS, nix-darwin, home-manager, etc.) converted to modular services than I care about these details.

This pull request has been mentioned on **NixOS Discourse**. There might be relevant details there:

https://discourse.nixos.org/t/should-we-expose-the-type-for-modular-services/73751/1

pull_request.title: Modular services: no `pkgs`

review_comments.body:
Is there a way to avoid having to list out all the dependencies for the service in the package file?

I'm thinking of something similar to `callPackage` when doing the `importApply ./service.nix`?
Yes, that should work, except we'll need to use `setFunctionArgs` because these aren't normal functions; it needs that change in `importApply`, or in a new helper.

I have strong doubts that gluing services to packages is a good idea. For context and additional detail see [my argument](https://discourse.nixos.org/t/nix-ngi-report-for-2025q1-2025-01-13-2025-04-15/63859) on establishing a notion of "application" that would *have* a "package as defined by Nix (i.e. files with metadata)" and a service module, and whatever else. From that point of view, it's hard to go along with this change, as it complicates invocation for what I consider to be the default scenario -- as a user, I don't want to set `package` explicitly every time I construct a modular service. The argument that one can mix Nixpkgs instances is of questionable value, because you can always do that by overriding a `package` from some calling context that has that alternative Nixpkgs around.
review_comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -12,18 +12,44 @@
   nodes = {
     server =
       { pkgs, ... }:
+      let
+        # Normally the package services.default attribute combines this, but we
+        # don't have that, because this is not a production service. Should it be?

review_comments.body:
> because you can always do that by overriding a package from some calling context that has that alternative Nixpkgs around.

Not _always_!
We'd have to accept conditional on version in some modules, but that's not how any of the codebases are typically set up, whether that's Nixpkgs, or third party repos/flakes. Almost all of those assume that they only have to deal with the `package` version that's in tree or pinned in tree.

> as a user, I don't want to set `package` explicitly every time I construct a modular service.

What is the friction?
For the user (configuration), they have to identify the service somehow, and `pkgs.foo.services.default` looks fine to me. We could even make that `pkgs.foo.service` if we don't care about "schema" uniformity as much.

Is it friction for the module author? We could reduce indirections and define modules with `finalPackage` and omit the `package` option.
Since we can't guarantee version interoperability for all services, perhaps we should just get rid of this `package` indirection?
